context:
NorthstarFleet is a fictional maintenance network resolving fleet-owning organizations across daily partner feeds. The master identifies legal organizations, not vehicles or depot locations. The batch system uses pair scoring and connected components, then assigns the smallest source row number as the entity ID. Clients cache these IDs in work orders. Sources can correct names, retract records or reuse local row numbers. There is no versioned lineage between a source row and an issued entity ID.

A proposed incremental updater revisits only immediate neighbors of a changed row. It promises to preserve the current entity ID whenever any old member remains, even after a split. Engineers have not established dependency closure when candidate features, accepted edges, membership or master fields change. A deletion request may require removal of personal contact fields, but retention and ID tombstone policy are still awaiting legal confirmation. Nightly full recomputation is available as a bounded comparison baseline on an isolated snapshot, although its current ID assignment is itself unstable.

Provide a design and experiment note, not an implementation. Compare full recomputation with a closure-aware incremental alternative and distinguish equivalence of resolution from stability of externally issued IDs. Address merges, splits, corrections, source-key reuse, retractions, provenance and downstream aliases or tombstones. State what can be replayed, which invariants need checking at pair, entity and lifecycle levels, and where missing authority or closure proof blocks action. Define safe next steps and explicit uncertainty.
title: NorthstarFleet stable organization IDs
